p01.why: A deleted function must not have another definition.

p03.why: Overload resolution selects the deleted f(double) for 1.5.

p04.why: The deleted constructor still takes part, so take(Gate) beats the ellipsis, and the call then uses the deleted constructor.

p05.why: A function that is not a special member or comparison operator cannot be defaulted.

p07.why: A reason in parentheses after delete is rejected under -pedantic-errors.

p08.why: Declaring a deleted function that nobody uses is valid.

p09.why: decltype and sizeof refer to the deleted f even though they do not evaluate it.

p11.why: A deleted function is inline, so the same deleted definition can be in both units, and other returns 0.

p12.why: GCC 14 accepts a deleted main, and GCC 16, Clang, and EDG reject it.

p13.why: A friend comparison operator declared in the class can be defaulted.

p14.why: delete is not on the first declaration.

p15.why: put(1) selects the exact match put(int), which is deleted.

p16.why: The deleted conversion function makes take(int) better than the ellipsis, and the call then uses the deleted conversion.

p17.why: Taking the address refers to the deleted f.
